title: Bioinspired microcapsule reactor with engineered probiotics for IBD therapy
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72027-1

The authors developed a bionic microcapsule containing engineered bacteria that sense gut inflammation and release targeted therapy. Microcapsule treatment in mouse model of inflammatory bowel disease restored intestinal barrier function.

title: Atmospheric CO₂-to-acetaldehyde artificial photosynthesis in metallo hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75384-z

This study develops metallo hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HNNU-X), which overcome the low CO2 concentration in air and sluggish proton transfer kinetics, achieving artificial photosynthesis of acetaldehyde from air, water and natural sunlight.

title: Pervasive summertime nitrous oxide undersaturation in U.S. lakes and reservoirs
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74705-6

A new study finds that 73% of US lakes and reservoirs function as N2O sinks during the summer, but uncertainty in large lake N2O concentrations precludes a determination of whether US lakes and reservoirs function as a net source or sink of atmospheric N2O.

title: Efficiency-weighted cooling degree days reveal opposing temperature and humidity effects on energy demand
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75388-9

A metric shows air conditioners work less efficiently as temperatures rise, while humidity can worsen or offset losses. Across North America, future cooling energy demand may grow far faster than standard temperature-based estimates suggest.

title: Phage portal proteins counteract stringent-response–mediated restriction
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75532-5

Bacteria can protect themselves against viral infections by entering physiological states, such as the stringent response, that limit cellular resources. Here, the authors show that phages can use their portal proteins to suppress the bacterial stringent response, thus promoting infection.

title: The traffic concentration effects of urban navigation services
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75254-8

Navigation services concentrate traffic onto a few roads as adoption increases. Simulations in Florence, Milan, and Rome show route diversity drops by up to 14% at full adoption, and CO2 benefits vanish or reverse beyond a city- and service-specific threshold.

title: Gapless fracton quantum spin liquid and emergent photons in a 2D spin-1 model
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74797-0

Gapless fracton quantum spin liquids described by higher rank gauge theories have remained elusive in microscopic quantum spin models. Here, the authors demonstrate a spin 1 square lattice model exhibiting signatures of a rank 2 U(1) fracton quantum spin liquid, including suppressed pinch points and emergent photon like excitations revealed by Green function Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Mesoscale ordered assembly of Er<sup>3+</sup>-doped quantum dots enables efficient 1.55 µm electroluminescence
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75429-3

Efficient 1.55 micrometer light sources are needed for telecom and infrared photonics, but realizing them with perovskite quantum dots is challenging due to bandgap limitations. Li et al. used Er3 + -doping and hydrogen-bonded ordered assembly in CsPbCl3 to enable efficient electroluminescence.
